scope: Every Realtek NIC that is up on a production PC with a Dante leg (docs/two-networks.md, scope). One entry per chip and OS; a Realtek adapter without an entry fails until it is measured and added. Read-only checkers: tools/windows/nic-standard-check.ps1, tools/linux/nic-standard-check.py.

fields.match: windows: hardware_id prefixes (the device's first hardware id, case-insensitive) or descriptions; linux: usb or pci vendor:product ids
fields.driver: windows: files (the allowed DriverFileName), min_version, bad (a file, or a file and version, that fails); linux: modules, firmware
fields.expected: a string, or a list of strings any of which passes; null with status report
fields.compare: equals (default), bits (every bit of expected is set), contains (the value holds the expected text)
fields.absent: fail (default): the keyword must be there; pass: a driver without the keyword passes
fields.status: settled: decided with its evidence; open: the standard value until the named measurement decides; report: no standard value yet, printed, never a failure
fields.profile: low_latency: checked only with the low_latency profile (iemmixer gen3, dasio); every other value holds for every profile
fields.evidence: a ticket, a measurement or a vendor document; 'none yet: fleet value' where the working PCs already share the value and nothing measured it

adapters.covers: RTL8156 and RTL8156B (USB 2.5GbE): one USB id. Every one in the fleet is an RTL8156B (bcdDevice 0x31xx; Realtek's 1156.22 INF matches REV_31F4 to its RTL8156B section; Linux firmware rtl8156b-2). No RTL8156 (non-B) is in use.

bad.evidence: Microsoft's inbox NetAdapterCx driver 11.4.211.2022: a 3-URB / 18-buffer send queue, no PendingTransmits keyword; 6400-9700 late Dante packets a busy minute at dsg against 198 an hour on 11.19.602.2025 at 8 / 64 (dstack #425, songplayer#337)
Realtek's NDIS driver 10.68.20: USB/WDF DPCs up to 19.3 ms against 0.28 ms on the Cx driver, A/B on mbc 18.11.2026 (dstack #290)

driver.evidence: Realtek's NetAdapterCx driver 11.19.602.2025 carries the transmit-queue keywords and measured clean against the inbox driver (dstack #425, songplayer#337); the Cx family against NDIS (dstack #290). Fleet: resolume-snv and resolume-pp.

values.name: Transmit URBs
values.evidence: 3 -> 8 (with buffers 18 -> 64): receivers' reorders ~9/h -> ~3/h, the FOH card's peak 9.6 -> 4.7 ms (dstack receiver A/B 10.11.2026, songplayer#255/#285); inbox 3 -> 8 cut dsg's late packets ~100x (dstack #425).
values.plan: 8 vs 32 on resolume-pp with two NDI receivers, by #425's ndiD capture (pktmon on TCPIP / NetAdapterCx / miniport, a detached 60 s capture, .claude/rules/windows-pcs.md): Dante TCPIP -> miniport p99 against 9.4 ms and max against 18.4 ms at 8; the value with the lower p99 and max becomes the standard.

values.name: Transmit Buffers
values.evidence: with PendingTransmits: the same A/B (songplayer#255/#285, dstack #425)

values.name: Flow Control
values.evidence: a PAUSE stops the NIC's whole send queue, Dante included (dstack #425); docs/two-networks.md

values.name: Energy-Efficient Ethernet
values.evidence: power saving off on every wired NIC (owner 7.11.2026, songplayer#285); docs/two-networks.md

values.name: Allow the computer to turn off this device: off

adapters.covers: RTL8156 and RTL8156B (USB 2.5GbE), as on Windows

driver.evidence: stream-snv runs Realtek's out-of-tree r8152 v2.21.4, stream-pp the kernel's; both lose rx_missed bursts next to near-line-rate video (dstack #408). The A/B of the two drivers decides; until then either passes and the version is printed.
driver.plan: dstack #408: the in-tree r8152 against v2.21.4 on stream-pp under the same JPEG XS load, rx_missed steps over a working day

values.name: RX interrupt coalescing
values.evidence: the driver's default, 15 us (the in-tree driver reads it in ns: 15000; v2.21.4 in us: 15). Any ethtool -C on a running r8152 link restarts the MAC (~2 s without Dante, docs/two-networks.md #290)

values.evidence: a PAUSE stops the whole send queue (dstack #425)

adapters.covers: Realtek PCIe 2.5GbE (RTL8125, 'Realtek Gaming 2.5GbE Family Controller') and GbE (RTL8111/8168, 'Realtek PCIe GbE Family Controller'): one driver (rt640x64), one INF, one entry

bad.evidence: 20-30 ms receive DPC every ~100 s on the RTL8125 (dasio#1, FOH 2.11.2026; dstack lso.rs REALTEK_BAD)

driver.evidence: 10.79.20.1003 measured best on FOH's RTL8125 with dasio's deferred receive and kernel TX; the inbox rtcx21 and 10.39 worse (dasio#1, dasio's baseline pin); clean on dsg's RTL8168 (dstack #383). 10.79.50.1003 on dsg's RTL8168s since 18.11 (owner ROZHODNUTE on dasio#120, dasio#188: SoundGrid clock losses 78 -> 0).
driver.plan: one version for the family: 10.79.50.1003 on FOH's RTL8125 too (dasio's step, dasio#120's rule: newer drivers are tested and deployed), then min_version 10.79.50.1003. dstack's start-line verdict (lso.rs REALTEK_BAD names 10.79.20.1003) is reconciled with dasio#1's later measurement.

values.name: Receive Buffers
values.evidence: dasio's baseline (the Dante NIC as tuned on FOH, dasio#1); on the RTL8168 4096 is above the INF's range (32-512) and what the driver applies is not measured
values.plan: on the RTL8168 (dsg), 4096 against the INF maximum 512, dasio's late and missed counts and a WPR DPC trace per hour (dasio's PC, dasio runs it); the RTL8125 (FOH) keeps 4096, inside its range 32-4096

values.name: Transmit Buffers
values.evidence: dasio's baseline (dasio#1); on the RTL8168 above the INF's range (32-128). docs/windows-box.md's 'at the driver's minimum' was a next step, never measured
values.plan: on the RTL8168 (dsg), 4096 against the INF maximum 128, the same A/B; the RTL8125 (FOH) keeps 4096, inside its range 64-4096
